decks.name: D1 Quintorius Spirits
decks.notes: Lorehold spirit recursion. Fill the graveyard with cheap instants, sorceries and artifacts, then turn each one into a 3/2 Spirit and cast it again for free. The graveyard is the resource, not a byproduct.

decks.name: D2 Chulane Value Loop
decks.notes: Creature-flood value. Every creature spell draws a card and drops a land, so board, mana and hand all grow on the same trigger. The deck wins by simply doing more per turn than anyone else.

decks.name: D3 Atraxa Proliferate
decks.notes: Proliferate control. Land a counter on anything that matters, then add to every counter on the board each end step until the accumulated advantage ends the game. The pod's control seat.

decks.name: D4 Felothar Walls

slots.optionWhy: Four basics come out for the two dorks and two rocks coming in (any four)
Four basics come out for the two dorks and two rocks coming in (any four)

decks.notes: Toughness fortress. Creatures deal combat damage equal to toughness and ignore defender, so the same permanents that hold the ground are the offense. Nothing in the deck is a dead card on either side of the table.

decks.name: D5 Shadrix Aristocrats
decks.notes: Token drain. Shadrix fires two modes every combat, flooding the board with evasive bodies while draining the table. Wins through the air and through incremental life loss rather than through combat math.

decks.name: D6 Krenko Goblins

slots.optionWhy: Trim one; the deck runs mana-heavy at 33

decks.notes: Goblin go-wide. Krenko doubles the board every activation, then a damage payoff converts bodies into a win without needing combat to connect. The fastest clock in the pod.

decks.name: D7 Maralen Exile Cast
decks.notes: Sultai exile-and-cast value, deliberately green-blue forward with black as the answer suite. Kept entirely off proliferate and +1/+1 counters so it never competes with Atraxa for cards or for a role at the table. Wins on card advantage, not board dominance.
